data.content_ref: inline:{"analogy":null,"claim":"As n grows, the probability of reaching unanimous consensus tends to 0. The finite obstruction structures are locally stable mixed configurations in which the set of edges connecting opposite colors is a matching: every vertex has at most one opposite-color neighbor, so each monochromatic induced subgraph has minimum degree at least 2 and its components contain cycles. The expected number of such stable mixed configurations grows like exp(c n) for some c>0, so the probability that the dynamics avoids all traps and reaches consensus is at most exp(-c n).","counterconditions":[{"case":"If the basin of attraction of the two consensus states occupies a 1-o(1) fraction of configurations despite exponentially many stable mixed states, then consensus probability would tend to 1.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"},{"case":"If stable mixed configurations are not reachable from typical initial colorings because their basins are exponentially small, the conclusion fails.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"}],"definitions":[],"derivation":[],"formalization_refs":[],"mechanism":"Each majority update strictly increases the number of monochromatic edges, so the process is absorbed in a local maximum of monochromatic edges. Stable mixed configurations are exactly cuts whose crossing edges form a matching; on a random 3-regular graph there are exponentially many such cuts because one can independently choose cycle components of each color and match them across a sparse set of edges. Starting from a uniform random coloring, the process is likely to hit one of these exponentially many absorbing traps before eliminating all crossing edges, so consensus is exponentially unlikely.","premises":[],"schema":"deepreason-reasoning-envelope-v1","scope":{"covers":[],"excludes":[]},"simulation_refs":[],"uncertainties":[]}
